messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: P0 SmartRouting errors spiking — 5xxs across EU and APAC egress. paging oncall (raj-patel). link: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-12345
ops-bot: alert summary: 4.2% error rate global, 12% in eu-west. latency up ~80ms for model requests. automatic rollback attempted for canary policy v3 -> fell back to fallback-variant which appears unhealthy.
raj-patel: I'm on it. taking pager. can someone drop the most recent smart-routing policy id?
keith-ong: Policy is smartroute-v3 (id: sr-2026-04-11-7). config shows fallback_variant: "redwood-large-v1-quant" and region_preference: [eu, apac, na]
anika-singh: That fallback_variant looks wrong — we onboarded redwood-large-v1 non-quant for hosted. quant variant was removed last week during model cleanup.
mike-hu: Observing a bunch of 502s from edge proxies in eu-west-1. Grafana: https://grafana.example/board/SmartRouteErrors
sara-liu: customer impact: churn-risk signals from two customers (ACME, NeonPay). approx 18% of their requests returning 502/503 in last 10m.
raj-patel: hypothesis: policy fallback referenced a removed model variant which triggers routing to incompatible endpoints. but why are 502s across regions?
keith-ong: I see in the routing logs requests that should go to eu compute are getting routed to apac edge VIPs, then back to eu — looks like a fallback loop. sample trace: 
```
route decision: eu-primary -> not available -> fallback-> apac-secondary -> healthcheck fail -> fallback -> eu-primary
```
anika-singh: Could be stale DNS rrset at the edge causing healthchecks to think primary is up when it's not. I've seen propagation delays leave old VIPs DNS records for ~TTL window.
mike-hu: Running dig against edge VIP: `dig +short vip.eu.service.redwood.net` returns both old-ip and new-ip for some resolvers. TTL is 30s but some caches still returning old rrset.
raj-patel: timeline: at 01:03 UTC routing policy v3 rollout started. at 01:06 we got first 5xx. at 01:09 automatic fallback kicked in. by 01:12 rate climbed.
skeith-ong: There's also a config mismatch: smartroute agent uses dns-cache TTL override=300s on some proxies (legacy). that explains why some proxies hold stale rrset beyond authoritative TTL.
anika-singh: mitigation plan: 1) disable smartroute rollouts (stop further policy pushes) 2) pin impacted customers to known-good model variant (redwood-large-v1) 3) purge DNS caches on edge proxies 4) update policy to avoid circular fallback.
raj-patel: do it. mike please run cache purge + healthcheck reset on eu and apac edges. keith, prepare policy revert. anika, coordinate with infra to purge DNS.
mike-hu: running command on eu proxies: 
```
for p in $(proxy-list --region eu-west-1); do ssh $p 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-proxy && sudo /usr/local/bin/dns-cache flush'; done
```
starting now. will report back in 60s.
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: rollback of smartroute-v3 -> smartroute-v2 initiated by keith-ong at 01:20 UTC. Status: in-progress.
keith-ong: rollback complete. smartroute-v2 active. policies pinned for customer clusters ACME and NeonPay to redwood-large-v1.
ram: (reaction) :thumbsup:
anika-singh: infra purged edge DNS caches and manually removed stale rrset from the geo-dns pool. authoritative now only returns new-ip.
mike-hu: After restart/purge, 502s dropped from 12%->1.1% in eu within 90s. Latency normalized.
sara-liu: Notifying account teams for ACME/NeonPay. Logging incident impact: 12% errors for 16 minutes for ACME, 9% for NeonPay.
raj-patel: root cause: smartroute-v3 referenced a decommissioned quantized model variant. fallback policy combined with inconsistent DNS caches produced a routing oscillation between regions. two contributing factors: a) model variant cleanup not gated against active policies, b) edge dns-caching TTL override inconsistent across fleet.
keith-ong: Postmortem action items (quick list): 1) Block model-variant deletion if referenced by active routing policies. 2) Normalize dns-cache TTL behavior across proxies (remove override). 3) Add safeties in smartroute: prefer single-fallback step and cooldown before re-eval. 4) Add synthetic canary traffic test for cross-region fallback.
anika-singh: I'll own item 2. timeline estimate 2 days to roll config.
keith-ong: I'll own item 1 and 3. need research on model registry hooks + policy validator.
raj-patel: I'll draft interim customer comm stating mitigation and ETA for full fix.
ops-bot: incident severity downgraded to P2 at 01:35 UTC. Postmortem assign: raj-patel, keith-ong, anika-singh.
mike-hu: follow-up: found ~120 proxies still running dns-cache TTL override=300 in prod. creating infra PR to remove.
sara-liu: thanks all — leaving notes for oncall handoff to morning team. I'll add timeline and impact to incident board.
raj-patel: handing off to daytime oncall (keith-ong). leaving at 01:52 UTC.
keith-ong: taking post-incident monitoring. will watch for recurrence for next 4 hours and loop in infra if any anomalies.
ops-bot: incident closed (automated) at 01:59 UTC.
summary: SmartRouting rollout referenced removed model variant combined with inconsistent edge DNS caches. Caused cross-region fallback loops and 5xx spike affecting customers ACME and NeonPay. Rollback to smartroute-v2 and DNS cache purge mitigated impact. Action items: block variant deletion when referenced, normalize DNS TTL behavior, add smartroute safeties, canary tests.
